name: Michigan

agency.name: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)

gaps: The registration tax is computed on the manufacturer's suggested base list price published by the Secretary of State; when the MSRP is not typed, the engine uses the price, which understates the tax of a discounted new car and of any used car.
A new plate expires on the owner's birthday, so the first registration is prorated by month; the engine shows a 12-month amount.

The electric and plug-in hybrid fees follow the motor fuel tax, re-indexed every January 1; only the 2026 amounts ($267 and $113) are published, so a renewal in 2027 or later is shown without an amount.
On a private sale the 6% use tax is computed on the price declared; the Department of Treasury makes the final determination.
The optional Recreation Passport ($15 a year) offered with registration is not added.
The $2.25 regulatory fee and $5.75 administration fee expire on October 1, 2027 under current law; the engine keeps them through 2027 and drops them for later years.

summary.docFeeNote: Documentary preparation fee capped at 5% of the cash price or $280, whichever is less (DIFS Bulletin 2025-03-CF); it is taxable.
summary.inspectionWhere: Michigan has no safety or emissions inspection for passenger cars.

params._src: tax: dealer-manual, trade-in; title: title-transfer; reg: mcl-801; ev: ev-fee

singular: Michigan's plate fee for a 1984 or newer car is a tax on the list price: $178 a year at $30,000, plus $6 for each $1,000 or fraction above [mcl-801].
The plate tax falls only three times: 90% of the first-year tax in the second year, then 90% of that, then 90% again for every later year [mcl-801].
Until October 1, 2027, each plate also carries a $2.25 regulatory fee and a $5.75 transportation administration fee [mcl-801].
The trade-in credit against the 6% sales tax was $5,000 in 2019 and grows by $1,000 every January, so it reaches $12,000 in 2026 and becomes unlimited once it would exceed $14,000 [trade-in].
The documentary preparation fee a dealer may charge is capped at 5% of the cash price or $280, whichever is less, under the 2025 adjustment [doc-fee].
A title transfer costs $15 and the sales or use tax is 6 percent; a $15 late fee applies after 15 days [title-transfer].
Electric cars pay $267 a year on top of the plate fee and plug-in hybrids $113, because the fuel tax rose on January 1, 2026 [ev-fee].
The electric surcharge is tied to the gasoline tax by law: $5 for each cent above 19 cents a gallon for an EV, $2.50 for a plug-in hybrid [mcl-801].
The Department of State tells dealers that the documentary preparation fee is taxable and goes on the title application with the other taxable charges [doc-tax].
Most plates expire on the owner's birthday and can be renewed up to six months in advance [ev-fee].

mcl-801.name: MCL 257.801, Registration taxes (Michigan Vehicle Code)
mcl-801.quote: More than $30,000.00, the tax of $178.00 is increased by $6.00 for each $1,000.00 increment or fraction ... (ii) For the second registration, 90% of the tax ... (a) A regulatory fee of $2.25 ... (b) A fee of $5.75 ... $5.00 per each 1 cent above 19 cents per gallon.

trade-in.name: MCL 205.51, General Sales Tax Act definitions (gross proceeds, trade-in credit)
trade-in.quote: Beginning January 1, 2019 ... the lesser of the following: (I) $5,000.00 ... Beginning January 1, 2020 and each January 1 thereafter, the amount ... is increased by an additional $1,000.00 each year.

dealer-manual.name: Michigan Department of State, Dealer Manual, Chapter 8: Sales Tax (revised April 2026)
dealer-manual.quote: When sales tax is due, the amount levied to a Michigan customer is 6% of the full purchase price of the vehicle.

doc-fee.name: Michigan DIFS, Bulletin 2025-03-CF, Documentary Preparation Fee
doc-fee.quote: the documentary preparation fee shall not exceed 5% of the cash price of the motor vehicle or $280.00, whichever is less.

doc-tax.name: Michigan Department of State, Dealer Manual, Chapter 7: RD-108 (revised June 2026)
doc-tax.quote: The documentary preparation fee is taxable and is entered on line 2 of the RD-108.

title-transfer.name: Michigan Department of State, Title transfer and vehicle registration
title-transfer.quote: $15 title transfer fee ... 6 percent sales tax ... $15 late fee if the title isn’t transferred within 15 days of the sale.

ev-fee.name: Michigan Department of State, FAQs: Vehicle tabs and license plates
ev-fee.quote: The EV fee is $267 and is charged in addition to any regular registration fees. The EV fee for trucks and buses is $367. The PHEV fee is $113 and is charged in addition to the regular registration fees.

fuel-tax.name: MCL 207.1008, Motor fuel tax rate
fuel-tax.quote: Beginning January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026, the cents-per-gallon rate on motor fuel is equal to the product of 51 cents multiplied by 1 plus the lesser of 0.05 or the inflation rate
